newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end strongly higher, volume soars.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end strongly higher, volume soars.

text.p: Brazilian stocks surged to close strongly higher on a flood of fresh capital and boosted by Wall Street as investors rushed to snap up benchmark Telebras and other blue chips, brokers said.
"It was strong. There was just a lot of demand and a lot of money coming in," said one local broker.

The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 48 most-traded shares ended up 1.57 percent at 11,133 points, led by a surge in Telebras preferred and common shares, on volume totalling 1.034 billion reais ($975 million).
Brokers said investors, egged on by afternoon gains on Wall Street, swooped in to buy Telebras amid rumors of exceptionally strong bids for Brazil's soon-to-be-privatized B Band cellular concessions.
"The Dow Jones helped a little, but basically it was Telebras," a dealer said. "It was the firmest paper today."
Preferred shares of Telebras, which also has cellular components and is due to be privatized, closed up 2.84 percent at 145.00 reais, while its common ended 3.32 percent higher at 136.90 reais.

Dealers said trade was especially intense in Telebras, which normally accounts for 60 to 65 percent of daily trade in Sao Paulo. But while it dragged the rest of the bourse higher, some key issues bucked the session's rising trend.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most-traded power stocks closed down 1.62 percent at 2,852 points, led by a 3.13 percent drop in Copel common.
But other major power sector shares also dropped, including a 3.13 percent drop in blue chip Eletrobras preferred to 514.00 reais and Eletropaulo preferred, which fell 1.01 percent to 147.50 reais.
A day ahead of the sale of 33 percent stake in Minas Gerais state's Cemig power firm, its preferred fell 1.21 percent to end at 48.80 reais, while its comon stayed flat at 48.00 reais.
Among top blue chips, state oil firm Petrobras' preferred also ended flat at 244.00 reais, while Cia Vale do Rio Doce's preferred declined 0.81 percent to end at 24.50 reais.
